title: Can Alignment Healthcare (ALHC) Climb 32.61% to Reach the Level Wall Street Analysts Expect?
content:
Shares of Alignment Healthcare (ALHC) have gained 3.2% over the past four weeks to close the last trading session at $19.26, but there could still be a solid upside left in the stock if short-term price targets of Wall Street analysts are any indication. Going by the price targets, the mean estimate of $25.54 indicates a potential upside of 32.6%.

The average comprises 13 short-term price targets ranging from a low of $19.00 to a high of $30.00, with a standard deviation of $2.82. While the lowest estimate indicates a decline of 1.4% from the current price level, the most optimistic estimate points to a 55.8% upside. More than the range, one should note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.

While the consensus price target is highly sought after by investors, the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable. And investors making investment decisions solely based on this tool would arguably do themselves a disservice.

But, for ALHC, an impressive average price target is not the only indicator of a potential upside. Strong agreement among analysts about the company's ability to report better earnings than they predicted earlier strengthens this view. While a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't gauge how much a stock could gain, it has proven to be powerful in predicting an upside.

Price, Consensus and EPS SurpriseZacks Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for ALHC

Here's What You Should Know About Analysts' Price Targets

According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.

While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?

They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.

However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.

Story Continues

That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.

Why ALHC Could Witness a Solid Upside

There has been increasing optimism among analysts lately about the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher. And that could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. After all, empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 16.9% over the past month, as three estimates have gone higher compared to no negative revision.

Moreover, ALHC currently has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), which means it is in the top 5% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much ALHC could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

title: Alignment Healthcare, Inc. Just Beat Analyst Forecasts, And Analysts Have Been Updating Their Predictions
content:
Shareholders might have noticed that Alignment Healthcare, Inc. (NASDAQ:ALHC) filed its first-quarter result this time last week. The early response was not positive, with shares down 4.1% to US$20.26 in the past week. Revenues were US$1.2b, approximately in line with whatthe analysts expected, although statutory earnings per share (EPS) crushed expectations, coming in at US$0.05, an impressive 502% ahead of estimates. The analysts typically update their forecasts at each earnings report, and we can judge from their estimates whether their view of the company has changed or if there are any new concerns to be aware of. We thought readers would find it interesting to see the analysts latest (statutory) post-earnings forecasts for next year.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.NasdaqGS:ALHC Earnings and Revenue Growth May 3rd 2026

Taking into account the latest results, the current consensus from Alignment Healthcare's twelve analysts is for revenues of US$5.18b in 2026. This would reflect a sizeable 22% increase on its revenue over the past 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to surge 82% to US$0.17. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of US$5.17b and earnings per share (EPS) of US$0.13 in 2026. Although the revenue estimates have not really changed, we can see there's been a considerable lift to earnings per share expectations, suggesting that the analysts have become more bullish after the latest result.

See our latest analysis for Alignment Healthcare

There's been no major changes to the consensus price target of US$25.54, suggesting that the improved earnings per share outlook is not enough to have a long-term positive impact on the stock's valuation. That's not the only conclusion we can draw from this data however, as some investors also like to consider the spread in estimates when evaluating analyst price targets. There are some variant perceptions on Alignment Healthcare, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at US$30.00 and the most bearish at US$19.00 per share. Analysts definitely have varying views on the business, but the spread of estimates is not wide enough in our view to suggest that extreme outcomes could await Alignment Healthcare shareholders.

Looking at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can make sense of these forecasts is to see how they measure up against both past performance and industry growth estimates. We can infer from the latest estimates that forecasts expect a continuation of Alignment Healthcare'shistorical trends, as the 30% annualised revenue growth to the end of 2026 is roughly in line with the 30% annual growth over the past five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in a similar industry are forecast to see their revenues grow 4.8% per year. So although Alignment Healthcare is expected to maintain its revenue growth rate, it's definitely expected to grow faster than the wider industry.

Story Continues

The Bottom Line

The most important thing here is that the analysts upgraded their earnings per share estimates, suggesting that there has been a clear increase in optimism towards Alignment Healthcare following these results. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. There was no real change to the consensus price target, suggesting that the intrinsic value of the business has not undergone any major changes with the latest estimates.

Following on from that line of thought, we think that the long-term prospects of the business are much more relevant than next year's earnings. We have estimates - from multiple Alignment Healthcare analysts - going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here.

title: ALHC Q1 Deep Dive: Membership Growth and Margin Expansion Offset by Cautious Guidance
content:
Health insurance company Alignment Healthcare (NASDAQ:ALHC) beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations in Q1 CY2026, with sales up 33.3% year on year to $1.24 billion. On the other hand, next quarter’s revenue guidance of $1.31 billion was less impressive, coming in 0.9% below analysts’ estimates. Its non-GAAP profit of $0.12 per share was 38.7% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

Is now the time to buy ALHC? Find out in our full research report (it’s free).

Alignment Healthcare (ALHC) Q1 CY2026 Highlights:

Revenue: $1.24 billion vs analyst estimates of $1.22 billion (33.3% year-on-year growth, 1.3% beat) Adjusted EPS: $0.12 vs analyst estimates of $0.09 (38.7% beat) Adjusted EBITDA: $37.85 million vs analyst estimates of $32.51 million (3.1% margin, 16.4% beat) The company slightly lifted its revenue guidance for the full year to $5.18 billion at the midpoint from $5.16 billion EBITDA guidance for the full year is $150.5 million at the midpoint, in line with analyst expectations Operating Margin: 1.3%, up from -0.6% in the same quarter last year Customers: 284,800, up from 236,300 in the previous quarter Market Capitalization: $4.66 billion

StockStory’s Take

Alignment Healthcare’s first quarter was marked by robust membership growth and improved operating margins, but the market response was negative, likely due to concerns over operational hiccups and the sustainability of recent gains. Management emphasized that strong sales execution and disciplined member retention were key to driving growth, with CEO John Kao noting, “Our results this quarter reflect strong execution across sales and member retention as well as our clinical operations.” The company also highlighted rapid progress in claims automation and technology investments as contributors to improved efficiency, though a temporary workflow issue related to inpatient admissions modestly pressured medical costs during the quarter.

Looking ahead, Alignment Healthcare’s updated guidance reflects a focus on scaling efficiently while managing cost pressures in a shifting policy environment. Management cited disciplined investments in automation and technology to improve claim processing, contract management, and clinical engagement. CFO James Head cautioned that while the company is investing in growth and infrastructure, it is maintaining a cautious approach to new member risk adjustment and product mix. The company plans to expand into additional markets but highlighted the need for operational readiness and ongoing scrutiny of policy changes, especially regarding Medicare Advantage rate updates and risk model evolutions.

Story Continues

Key Insights from Management’s Remarks

Management attributed the quarter’s performance to disciplined sales and retention, ongoing technology investments, and operational agility amid policy and workflow changes.

Membership expansion: The company experienced significant membership growth, driven by strong open enrollment performance and retention initiatives, with an emphasis on medically complex populations that benefit from Alignment’s clinical model. Claims automation progress: Investments in automation resulted in claims auto-adjudication rates rising from under 15% to over 60% year-over-year, reducing administrative costs and improving overall efficiency. Workflow disruption and resolution: A CMS rule change led to a temporary workflow issue—overpaying for certain hospital admissions—that was identified and corrected within a month, demonstrating the company’s ability to respond quickly to operational challenges. Shift toward higher acuity members: Growth in special needs populations (SNPs) was intentional, with management highlighting the long-term margin potential as these members mature and transition into the loyal customer base. Technology and AI investments: The company is deploying AI-driven contract management and clinical risk stratification tools, aiming to further reduce SG&A and medical care ratios while improving care quality and scalability.

Drivers of Future Performance

Alignment’s outlook centers on continued operational scaling, targeted investments in automation, and navigating regulatory changes affecting Medicare Advantage.

Scaling automation and AI: Management is prioritizing increased automation in claims and contract management, expecting these initiatives to enhance operational leverage and lower administrative expenses over time. Population mix and risk modeling: The company’s focus on acquiring more medically complex members may temporarily elevate medical costs, but management expects margin tailwinds as these members become established and as risk adjustment processes mature. Regulatory and policy headwinds: Ongoing changes in Medicare Advantage policies and risk model updates present uncertainties, with management highlighting the importance of adaptability as CMS pursues greater program accountability and cost containment.

Catalysts in Upcoming Quarters

In the coming quarters, the StockStory team will be monitoring (1) further improvements in claims automation and their impact on SG&A efficiency, (2) the integration and performance of new, higher-acuity members as they mature within the plan, and (3) Alignment Healthcare’s execution on entering new markets while maintaining disciplined cost controls. Developments in Medicare Advantage policy and risk model updates will also be key indicators of future performance.

Release Date: April 30, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.

Positive Points

Alignment Healthcare Inc (NASDAQ:ALHC) reported a 31% year-over-year increase in health plan membership, reaching 284,800 members. Total revenue for the first quarter of 2026 was $1.2 billion, representing a 33% increase year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA grew by 88% compared to the prior year, reaching $38 million, and exceeded the high end of the company's guidance range. The company improved its adjusted SG&A as a percentage of revenue by 60 basis points year-over-year to 8.7%. ALHC's claims auto adjudication rate increased from less than 15% to over 60% year-to-date, indicating significant progress in automation and efficiency.

Negative Points

The CMS rule change impacted ALHC's observation determination process, leading to higher inpatient admissions per thousand in the first quarter. Despite resolving the process change by the end of February, the first quarter inpatient admissions per thousand were in the high 150s, affecting financial performance. The company faced a temporary disruption in its utilization management process, which impacted adjusted gross profit. ALHC's focus on growth among high-acuity populations may lead to higher inpatient admissions per thousand, impacting medical costs. The company is cautious about risk adjustment for new members, which may limit revenue recognition until CMS provides updated paid files.

Q & A Highlights

Q: Can you explain the hospital observation issue and how it was resolved? A: John Kao, CEO: We had a workflow problem where authorizations were paid at full acute rates instead of observation rates. This was corrected by the end of January, impacting our January numbers by a couple of million dollars. It was an internal issue, not a utilization problem, and has been resolved. Utilization is tracking as expected.

Story Continues

Q: What are the expectations for the second quarter MBR, and how does it compare to the first quarter? A: James Head, CFO: The second quarter is typically better seasonally, leading to a natural decline in MBR. We expect improvements across all margins, including MBR, SG&A, and EBITDA. The first half of the year is expected to show strong performance with margin improvements, despite ongoing investments in the business.

Q: How are you approaching the potential changes in the CMS risk model and its impact on future operations? A: John Kao, CEO: We anticipate changes in the risk model, possibly by 2029. CMS aims to ensure coding is not a competitive advantage, which aligns with our focus on delivering high-quality outcomes at low costs. We believe this will benefit us in the long term.

Q: Can you provide more details on the inpatient issue and its resolution? A: John Kao, CEO: The issue was due to a CMS rule change requiring more timely authorizations. It was an internal workflow issue, not specific to any market, and has been corrected. We are continuously refining our processes to support growth and maintain performance.

Q: How are you managing risk adjustment with the focus on more medically complex members? A: James Head, CFO: We are cautious with new members, booking to the paid MMR from CMS. This provides potential upside in the second quarter when final sweeps occur. We are confident in our ability to manage risk adjustment effectively.

title: Alignment Healthcare forecasts $138M-$163M adjusted EBITDA for 2026 as membership outlook rises to 294,000-299,000
content:
Earnings Call Insights: Alignment Healthcare (ALHC) Q1 2026

MANAGEMENT VIEW

 	* CEO John Kao said Q1 “health plan membership of 284,800 represented year-over-year membership growth of approximately 31%” and said the quarter produced “total revenue of $1.2 billion,” “adjusted gross profit of $146 million,” and “adjusted EBITDA was $38 million,” adding that this “exceeded the high end of our guidance range.” 
 	* Kao described a Q1 utilization disruption tied to CMS rules and internal workflow execution, saying, “the CMS rule change impacted our observation determination process” and that “this process change was resolved by the end of February, but impacted our first quarter inpatient admissions per 1,000, which was in the high 150s this quarter.”
 	* Kao highlighted operational scaling initiatives, including, “just 12 months ago, our claims auto adjudication rate was less than 15%. Now our year-to-date auto adjudication rate is over 60%,” and said the company is “deploying contract management solutions that leverage AI” and “taking the next leap forward in our AVA AI risk stratification models.”
 	* CFO James Head said Q1 results included “revenue of $1.2 billion,” “adjusted gross profit of $146 million represented an MBR of 88.2%,” and “adjusted EBITDA of $38 million produced an adjusted EBITDA margin of 3.1%,” while noting “GAAP SG&A was $121 million” and “adjusted SG&A was $108 million.”

OUTLOOK

 	* CFO James Head guided Q2 revenue of $1.30B-$1.32B vs. analysts’ $1.31223527B, and full-year 2026 revenue of $5.16B-$5.21B (the transcript did not provide EPS guidance).
 	* Head raised full-year membership guidance to 294,000-299,000 and said, “we are increasing our membership growth expectation given continued strength within our sales operations and outperformance in member retention through the open enrollment period.”
 	* Head lifted the low end of profitability ranges, stating, “we are raising the low end of each of our adjusted gross profit and adjusted EBITDA guidance ranges by $5 million,” and said the model assumes “inpatient admissions per 1,000 will run higher year-over-year” due to “growth amongst high acuity populations.”

FINANCIAL RESULTS

 	* Q1 revenue was $1.2B vs. analysts’ $1.21765528B (the transcript did not provide Q1 EPS).
 	* CFO James Head said Q1 adjusted SG&A ratio improvement “outperformed the midpoint of our implied guidance range by 50 basis points” as “adjusted SG&A as a percentage of revenue declined…to 8.7%.”
 	* Head reported liquidity of “$726 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments” and said “the funded leverage ratio at the end of Q1 improved to 2.6x trailing 12-month EBITDA.”

Q&A

 	* Matthew Gillmor, KeyBanc: Asked what changed in the hospital observation issue and post-fix trends; Founder, CEO John Kao: “we paid authorizations at full acute rates when we should have paid them at observation rates…It was a workflow problem,” adding it “impacted our January numbers, a couple of million dollars”; CFO Head: “Absent that issue…we probably in the mid-150s…The flu…was pretty much in line…we see that in April as well.”
 	* John Stansel, JPMorgan: Asked about Q2 MBR improvement assumptions; CEO Kao: “second quarter is usually our seasonal better quarter,” and said first-half expectations include “MBR first half, 40 basis points…SG&A, 40 basis points…EBITDA is 90 basis points to 100 basis points.”
 	* Scott Fidel, Goldman Sachs: Pressed for details, scope by market, and clawbacks; CEO Kao: “the answer is unfortunately no” on clawbacks and tied the issue to “dedelegating certain IPAs”; CFO Head: “by the end of January, we saw a little bit of an anomaly…by February, we had identified it and already corrected it.”
 	* Benjamin Mayo, Leerink: Asked about risk adjustment on medically complex growth; CFO Head: “as it pertains to risk adjustment on the new members…we take a cautious stance,” adding “we book to the paid MMR.”
 	* Jessica Tassan, Piper Sandler: Asked about the GLP-1 “bridge model” pilot; CEO Kao: “we would participate with certain conditions,” but said it “gets into…our product strategy for the ’27 bids, which I’d like to not discuss at this point.”
 	* Andrew Mok, Barclays: Asked why lean into PPO and whether it becomes a bigger growth driver; CFO Head: “I don’t think we have figured out the secret sauce yet,” adding, “the unit economics are going to be pretty tough for people.”
 	* Craig Jones, BofA: Asked how to handle a 2.48% net rate context vs trend; CEO Kao: “No way trend is going to be at 2.48%,” and said “L.A. County’s rate increases are closer to 6%.”
 	* Ryan Daniels, William Blair: Asked about bringing supplemental benefits in-house; CEO Kao: “it’s an opportunity for us to lower MLR by bringing some of that in-house,” and said it is “not something we’re embedding into any of our thinking for the first half guidance.”

SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

 	* Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to neutral, with repeated probing on the utilization workflow disruption, MBR trajectory, rates/trend mismatch, and reserving; questions included “give us some sense for how hospital utilization trended,” and “is there an opportunity for you to claw back.”
 	* Management’s tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and more defensive/clarifying in Q&A on utilization, emphasizing scope and fixes; CEO Kao said, “It’s not a utilization issue,” and CFO Head repeatedly framed it as “a onetime course correction” and “corrective action.”
 	* Versus last quarter, management in Q1 used more operational-detail explanations (workflow, de-delegation, claims automation) while maintaining confidence language; CEO Kao said, “I feel really good about this year, guys. I really do,” compared with Q4’s emphasis on multi-year profitability transformation.

QUARTER-OVER-QUARTER COMPARISON

 	* Q1 introduced a discrete operational disruption (observation vs. acute authorization workflow) and described remediation timelines; Q4 did not cite a comparable internal process issue and instead emphasized navigating “the second phase of the V28 risk model” and “a redesign of the Part D program.”
 	* Guidance changed directionally upward on membership and revenue in Q1; CFO Head said, “we are increasing our membership growth expectation,” and “raising our full year revenue guidance,” compared with Q4’s initial 2026 ranges.
 	* Q1 analyst focus concentrated on utilization mechanics, MBR seasonality, and market expansion constraints, while Q4 questions leaned more toward rate-policy scenarios, AI use cases, and new-state provider engagement readiness.

RISKS AND CONCERNS

 	* Management flagged policy and operational execution risk, including “the CMS rule change” affecting utilization management workflows and the need to scale de-delegated functions as the company grows “outside of California.”
 	* CEO Kao highlighted rate/trend tension, stating “No way trend is going to be at 2.48%,” and framed mitigation through market-level positioning, including “L.A. County’s rate increases are closer to 6%.”
 	* CFO Head emphasized uncertainty around new-member risk adjustment timing, saying the company is “very cautious” and waits for “paid files” before recognizing potential upside.

FINAL TAKEAWAY

Management described Q1 as a quarter of faster growth and stronger profitability than expected, while calling out a corrected, one-month utilization management workflow issue tied to observation determinations. Leadership raised 2026 membership and revenue outlook and lifted the low end of adjusted gross profit and adjusted EBITDA guidance, while reiterating that growth is increasingly oriented toward higher-acuity populations and supported by scaling initiatives such as claims automation and AI-enabled workflows. In Q&A, analysts repeatedly pressed on utilization, rate adequacy, and product/market expansion, and management responded by emphasizing rapid detection and remediation, cautious risk-adjustment recognition for new members, and continued plans to expand into new markets in 2027 without detailing bid tactics.
